trust_decision.summary: A peer-controlled Host header value must never raise out of HTTP::Request#complete: the parse of 'Host' is turned into the request parser's error state (Headers#error), which Driver::Server#parse converts into a protocol-error/close event instead of an uncaught exception.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names a malformed Host header, and this is the only place a Host header value is handed to URI.parse; the crash comes from that call.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No alternate site exists; the nearest arguable dismissal is that the Client and Proxy drivers also call URI.parse (lib/websocket/driver/client.rb:21, lib/websocket/driver/proxy.rb:15-16) but on application-supplied URLs, not on peer-supplied headers.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate requests must still succeed: a request with no Host header is currently accepted (the block is skipped) and a valid Host with an explicit port must still populate SERVER_NAME/SERVER_PORT so that Server#url keeps working. A fix that requires a Host header, or restricts it to a bare hostname, breaks both.

O6_input_shapes: any single Host value that URI.parse rejects with URI::InvalidURIError (empty/whitespace value, illegal host or port characters); the published fix is shape-agnostic, one rescue covers all such values
duplicate Host headers, which the header parser joins into one comma-joined value before the URI parse (lib/websocket/http/headers.rb:101-106)
absent Host header - unchanged by the fix and still accepted (lib/websocket/http/request.rb:36)

O7_producer.where: lib/websocket/http/request.rb:31-35 (headers copied into @env inside complete, values produced by lib/websocket/http/headers.rb:95-107 in the same parse call)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second peer-header-derived env field built with URI.parse (e.g. normalising HTTP_ORIGIN or HTTP_REFERER into scheme/host/port alongside SERVER_NAME/SERVER_PORT)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This method exists only to synthesise Rack env fields from peer headers, so a maintainer adding another derived field would use the same idiom on the same peer-controlled strings.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Server#url validating/parsing HTTP_HOST with URI.parse before composing the WebSocket URL
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: url is public API consumed by Rack/EventMachine integrations, and the project has already had Host/port handling bugs on the client side (Driver.host_header, lib/websocket/driver.rb:216-222), so a maintainer could plausibly parse here too.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Peer response parsing in Proxy#parse never checks @http.error?, unlike Client#parse (lib/websocket/driver/client.rb:64-65)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the same 'turn malformed peer input into a protocol error' mechanism on another transport, and its omission is visible in a neighbouring implementation.

O9_family: uncaught exception on malformed peer input (CWE-248) leading to denial of service

O10_build.toolchain: bundler + rake-compiler (ext/websocket-driver/extconf.rb C extension, with pure-Ruby fallback in lib/websocket/mask.rb); rspec
O10_build.project_tests: rspec suite in spec/ (spec/websocket/driver/{hybi,draft75,draft76,client}_spec.rb) drives the protocol drivers from hand-built env hashes; there is no spec for HTTP::Request or Server#parse, so request-line/header parsing has no test coverage at the pinned commit.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Rescue the parse error locally and carry on without setting the parser's error state (or swallow the exception around the whole chunk in Server#parse), so the request is silently accepted with a nil SERVER_NAME instead of being failed with error+close.

out_of_scope_notes: On Ruby 3.1+ URI.parse returns no port for a default-port authority, so lib/websocket/http/request.rb:39 would set SERVER_PORT to "" for 'Host: example.com'; a separate latent issue, not pursued.
lib/websocket/driver/proxy.rb:49-62 never checks @http.error? while lib/websocket/driver/client.rb:65 does; unrelated inconsistency, not pursued.
unverified: Could not run Ruby (no shell), so which Host values raise URI::InvalidURIError versus another URI::Error subclass cannot be checked; if some malformed host:port values raise URI::InvalidComponentError, the published rescue (fix.diff:28) would leave that shape crashing at the same site.
The advisory's exact malformed Host example is not in the tree; input shapes are inferred from the fix and the header grammar.
repo_mb was not measured; tiny_repo is inferred from a tree of about 30 small source files.
Ruby-version-dependent URI#port behaviour behind the SERVER_PORT note is not verified in this environment.
